Mira: Nightly kernel-kbench sweep produced a weird flip in kernel picks around 1k->2k on H100, heatmap shows non-monotonic pick and a ~12% median latency hump. artifact: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/2369019999/heatmap.png :thinking:
PerfBot: nightly-run complete; artifacts uploaded -> https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/2369019999 (heatmap, raw-microbench, traces)
Alejandra: Can someone paste the exact harness invocation? I want to repro on my H100 node.
Jon: Repro command I used locally:
```
./kbench --model gpt2-xl --device h100 --seqlens 256,512,1024,2048 --kernels candidate_set.json --iters 250 --profile kv,latency
```
Summary I saw: seqlen 256 -> K_X (2.1ms), 512 -> K_X (3.0ms), 1024 -> K_Y (4.4ms), 2048 -> K_X (8.1ms)  <-- K_X comes back at 2048, unexpected vs earlier canary runs where K_Z dominated longseq. raw mapping: 256->K_X,512->K_X,1024->K_Y,2048->K_X
Ryan: My hypothesis: sampling + KV cache behavior is skewing measured throughput during autotune. If the harness samples a mixed workload with warm prefixes, kernels that are memory-friendlier look better even when miss-heavy traffic would favor a different kernel. Try forcing KV cache off to see baseline kernel perf.
Mira: Ran kbench with KV cache disabled and KV debug enabled. Cmd: `REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=0 KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1 ./kbench --model gpt2-xl --device h100 --seqlens 2048 --iters 250`
Trace excerpt:
```
[profiler] seqlen=2048 samples=250
kv_hit_rate=0.10 kv_miss_rate=0.90
measured_throughput_ms: K_X=7.9 K_Y=8.6 K_Z=7.4
autotune_score: K_X=0.98 K_Y=0.92 K_Z=1.00
selected=K_X (tie-break: lower memory footprint)
```
Alejandra: So autotuner scoring currently favors memory footprint tie-breakers and doesn't fold kv_miss penalty into the score. That explains why K_X wins under miss-heavy samples despite K_Z having better raw latency when misses are accounted for.
Sam: We should update scoring function to compute an effective latency that includes kv miss penalty. Proposed: `effective_latency = measured_latency + kv_miss_rate * kv_miss_penalty_ms + memory_penalty_ms`. Then pick kernel with lowest effective_latency. Also add unit tests for cold/warm/miss-heavy profiles.
Jon: Quick prototype I tested locally (pseudocode):
```
score = 1.0 / (measured_throughput_ms + kv_miss_rate * kv_penalty_ms + memory_penalty_ms)
```
Works on my node for the candidate set: K_Z becomes best for miss-heavy profile, K_X still best for warm profile.
Mira: Please open an issue and assign runtime oncall. Also let's gate this in perf CI: nightly kbench sweep should run three KV profiles per seqlen (warm, mixed, cold/miss-heavy) and produce a stacked heatmap + delta assertions.
CI-Bot: Created perf job `kernel-kbench-kvprofiles-nightly` and scheduled the first run 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z.
Sam: Plan: 1) small scoring change + tests, 2) add KV-profiles to harness + aggregator for heatmaps, 3) backfill last 30 nightlies to detect regression window, 4) run gating on H100 and Ampere candidate sets. I'll open PRs for (1) and (2) shortly. :thumbsup:
Mira: Assigned ISSUE-412 (runtime: kernel-autotune-kv-weighting) to @runtime-oncall and added P0 label. Link: https://tracker.internal/redwood/ISSUE-412
Alejandra: One more note: autotune sampling window should record kv_hit_rate and sampling batch size used for scoring so we can replay exact conditions during CI. Otherwise reproduce is hard.
Jon: Adding logs and a small CLI flag `--autotune-debug` that emits per-kernel `{kv_hit_rate, batch_size, measured_latency}` to artifacts. Will include in PR.
Ryan: After the scoring change we should re-run the historical artifacts to compute where the flip started. If it's a recent regression, we can cherry-pick a fix and patch nightlies.
Sam: Agreed. I'll include a backfill script in the PR that scans artifacts and computes preferred-kernel deltas across SVs.
Mira: Thanks all. Triage notes posted in ISSUE-412. Let's ensure the CI gating asserts median latency regression <=5% across profiles or it fails.
Sam: Opening PRs now; will ping this thread with links.
(ends)
